cross_cutting_findings: QA% bug found and fixed mid-session: an initial query returned 0% for every account (COUNT DISTINCT CASE WHEN logic error); corrected to COUNT DISTINCT ... THEN group_id. Real QA% varies enormously by account (0% to 100%) — this is the third time this exact 'reads as 0% due to a query bug' pattern has hit this rubric build (TES hit it earlier the same day too). Worth a standing sanity check before trusting any 0% out of this pipeline going forward.

Revenue Trend is fully blocked — REVENUE_ACTUAL_BI is not exposed via any Sigma workbook this connection can reach, and isn't discoverable by name search either. Needs a raw Snowflake grant or a different workbook, not more querying.

Several accounts show extremely high QA% (Brandywine 92.7%, Brick and Timber 90.6%, Standard Management 90.9%, Willowdale 92.6%, Rookwood 80.0%, Sentral 77.2%, Elme 100%) alongside high Support ratios. The Sigma agent's working assumption is these are legitimate PM-driven QA workflow policies, not a data bug — but that assumption hasn't been independently verified against product/CSM knowledge, and it's a big enough cluster to be worth a real answer rather than an assumption.

Two accounts (Harbor Group Parent 6.4%, Western Wealth Parent 6.8%) breach the rubric's >6% Override Rate hard-gate for ENT/MM, which per the rubric's own rule caps their composite score at Yellow regardless of every other metric.

Three accounts have effectively no usable data this pass: Standard Management Company Parent (n=4 decisioned groups, n=11 total groups), Willowdale/WPM (n=15-27 across metrics), and Elme Communities (n=13) — every metric on these three is noise-dominated, not a real signal.
Highmark and Standard Management Company Parent show NULL Volume Trend because they had zero groups in the prior-90-day window — likely recent activation/ramp, not a real trend.

CORRECTION to an earlier same-session claim that HubSpot has zero CSM-entered qualitative fields: a broader property scan found real infrastructure (at_risk, account_health_label, swan_score, Deal-object champion_* fields) that the first, narrower scan missed. BUT a follow-up data pull found those fields are 0% populated across all 20 in-scope accounts — the schema exists, nobody's using it. The only populated field is churn_risk__c, a frozen Salesforce snapshot from the 2026-07-10 migration cutover that predates this entire Q3 scoring window and is explicitly not maintained going forward. Net effect: the practical conclusion (no current, live qualitative risk data) is unchanged, but for a more nuanced reason than originally stated. Values are in each account's qualitative_pillars.strategic_alignment_governance field for historical context only.

Notable divergence: Evernest carries a frozen 'Red' churn-risk snapshot (matching a similarly Red manual flag in Notion) but this session's real Q3 platform-metrics pull shows Evernest mostly Green/Yellow, with only TES% (Red) and Volume Trend (Yellow) flagged. Two stale/manual sources agreeing with each other isn't independent confirmation — they likely both trace back to the same original Salesforce assessment. Harbor Group Parent shows the opposite pattern: a merely 'Yellow' frozen snapshot despite a real, current override-rate hard-gate breach (6.4%) that the snapshot has no way to know about.

approval_rate_pct.source: Sigma Core (Data Model), Groups BI, direct query, same population as TTD above.

override_rate_pct.source: Sigma Core (Data Model), Groups BI 'Has Decision Override' (W6x8udeWRR), direct query. Refreshed 2026-08-18 -- denominator/numerator reflect today's decisioned-this-quarter population, which grows daily; small movement vs. any earlier snapshot is expected QTD accrual, not a data error. Bands (ENT/MM): Green <=3%, Yellow 3-6%, Red >6% (reverse-engineered from the existing banded values across all 20 accounts, not a directly-quoted rubric threshold -- treat as provisional like the support-ticket-ratio recalibration). override_rate_pct.split_note: These two rows are NOT a decomposition of the blended rate above -- verified 2026-08-18 that they don't sum to it (e.g. Bridge Tower: blended=8 but approval+decline directional flags=0+0; Highmark: blended=7 but directional flags sum to 89). These are a different, narrower lens (did the group's own recorded outcome flip declined->approved, or approved->declined), not officially banded (no Green/Yellow/Red threshold has been defined for either direction individually) -- shown as raw rate/count only. Sourced from Sigma Core (Data Model), Groups BI: 'Group Is Decision Outcome Declined to Approved' (approval override) and 'Group Is Decision Outcome Approved to Declined' (decline override), same population as the blended row (GROUP_IS_DECISIONED=true AND GROUP_DECISIONED_AT >= 2026-07-01).

gong_call_sentiment.source: Sourced via direct Gong REST API (not the stale Salesforce Gong__Gong_Call__c sync, confirmed 5+ weeks behind as of 2026-08-18), domain-matched to account, trailing 90 days. Classified by reading each matched call's AI-generated brief against the account-health-weekly-review skill's 3-tier definition (Positive=milestones confirmed/proactive/no escalations, Neutral=routine sync/no strong signal, Negative=friction/frustration/unresolved bugs/Findigs blamed/competitor pressure). Accounts with zero domain-matched Gong calls in the window are left unscored (None) rather than assumed negative -- a coverage gap in domain-matching is not evidence of silence. 'thin' accounts had very few matched calls (1-3), so the classification rests on a small sample.

pylon_ticket_tone.source: Sourced via direct Pylon search_issues filtered to a confirmed exact account_id (resolved via search_accounts by domain/name, NOT the fuzzy account-name partial-match filter -- that filter was tested and found to cross-contaminate results across unrelated companies sharing generic name tokens, e.g. a 'Western Wealth' search surfaced 'Howard Management Group' and 'Group Fox Management' tickets; verified via get_issue on 3 sample tickets before trusting any count). States new/waiting_on_you/waiting_on_customer/on_hold, trailing ~90 days (created_after 2026-05-20). Counted only tickets flagging real PM-facing friction (tagged Escalated/Records Escalations, or title containing integration/config/migration/escalation/SOP/backlog-type keywords) per the account-health-weekly-review skill's PM-vs-renter title filter rule -- excludes the large majority of tickets, which are routine individual-applicant screening actions (income verification, co-applicants, ID disputes) and not a signal of PM relationship health. Classification: 0 friction tickets=Positive/Green, 1-2=Neutral/Yellow, 3+=Negative/Red. CAVEAT: raw-count based, not normalized by account ticket volume -- larger accounts (e.g. Beztak, McKinley, Highmark) are mechanically more likely to cross the 3+ threshold even at an equivalent underlying friction rate. This is an approximate keyword-based proxy for Tatiana's documented methodology, not a literal reproduction of undisclosed exact logic.

composite_score_partial.methodology: PARTIAL composite -- 16 of 19 rubric rows have real current data (the 3 missing rows -- Business goals, KPIs, NPS -- are listed in rows_missing_no_current_data; NPS has real data for only 7/20 accounts, all historical/pre-quarter). performance_review_cadence, executive_sponsor_alignment, and csm_qualitative_risk_flag were added 2026-08-18 (Gong-derived for the first two, HubSpot churn_risk__c for the third per Emma's direction); gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone were added 2026-08-18 (direct Gong API brief-reading and Pylon exact-account-id issue search, respectively, per Emma's sourcing direction from the account-health-weekly-review skill doc) -- see per-account 'note'/'source' fields on each for methodology caveats, several of which are best-effort proxies, not confirmed ground truth (in particular: gong_call_sentiment is unscored/None for 6 accounts with zero domain-matched Gong calls in the window -- a coverage gap, not a confirmed negative; pylon_ticket_tone is a raw-count-based proxy not normalized by account ticket volume, so larger accounts are mechanically more likely to land Red). Weight redistributed proportionally among available rows only (weights re-normalized to sum to rows_included_weight_sum, not literally 100). Per-metric scoring: Green=100/Yellow=50/Red=0, weighted average, per the pre-existing account-health-weekly-review skill's formula that this rubric explicitly carries forward. Floor rule (same skill), changed 2026-08-19 per Emma's direction to stop collapsing the displayed number: exactly 1 Red-banded row among those included still forces band=Yellow, and 2+ Red rows still forces band=Red, regardless of what the weighted math alone would say -- but as of 2026-08-19 'value' is ALWAYS the true weighted average, never overridden to a flat 50 or 0. This means a Red-banded account can show a value anywhere in 0-100 (e.g. a Red account with mostly-Green rows but 2 Red ones might still show in the 70s) -- the number is for relative severity/triage, the band is the categorical gate. (Previously, 2026-08-18 through 2026-08-19 morning: value WAS forced to a flat 0/50 to match the band -- changed after Emma flagged that this made every Red account look identical.) Decision Override Rate's Red band does NOT count toward this floor for SMB accounts, per the rubric's explicit 'not gated' rule for that segment. Bands when no floor applies: Green >=80, Yellow 60-79, Red <60 (matches both the rubric xlsx Overview tab and the skill's SKILL.md, confirmed 2026-08-18 via AskUserQuestion -- NOT the 0-33/33-66/66-100 scheme raised earlier in conversation and then not used).

composite_score_partial.methodology: PARTIAL composite -- 16 of 19 rubric rows have real current data (the 3 missing rows -- Business goals, KPIs, NPS -- are listed in rows_missing_no_current_data; NPS has real data for only 7/20 accounts, all historical/pre-quarter). performance_review_cadence, executive_sponsor_alignment, and csm_qualitative_risk_flag were added 2026-08-18 (Gong-derived for the first two, HubSpot churn_risk__c for the third per Emma's direction); gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone were added 2026-08-18 (direct Gong API brief-reading and Pylon exact-account-id issue search, respectively, per Emma's sourcing direction from the account-health-weekly-review skill doc) -- see per-account 'note'/'source' fields on each for methodology caveats, several of which are best-effort proxies, not confirmed ground truth (in particular: gong_call_sentiment is unscored/None for 6 accounts with zero domain-matched Gong calls in the window -- a coverage gap, not a confirmed negative; pylon_ticket_tone is a raw-count-based proxy not normalized by account ticket volume, so larger accounts are mechanically more likely to land Red). Weight redistributed proportionally among available rows only (weights re-normalized to sum to rows_included_weight_sum, not literally 100). Per-metric scoring: Green=100/Yellow=50/Red=0, weighted average, per the pre-existing account-health-weekly-review skill's formula that this rubric explicitly carries forward. Floor rule (same skill), changed 2026-08-19 per Emma's direction to stop collapsing the displayed number: exactly 1 Red-banded row among those included still forces band=Yellow, and 2+ Red rows still forces band=Red, regardless of what the weighted math alone would say -- but as of 2026-08-19 'value' is ALWAYS the true weighted average, never overridden to a flat 50 or 0. This means a Red-banded account can show a value anywhere in 0-100 (e.g. a Red account with mostly-Green rows but 2 Red ones might still show in the 70s) -- the number is for relative severity/triage, the band is the categorical gate. (Previously, 2026-08-18 through 2026-08-19 morning: value WAS forced to a flat 0/50 to match the band -- changed after Emma flagged that this made every Red account look identical.) Decision Override Rate's Red band does NOT count toward this floor for SMB accounts, per the rubric's explicit 'not gated' rule for that segment. Bands when no floor applies: Green >=80, Yellow 60-79, Red <60 (matches both the rubric xlsx Overview tab and the skill's SKILL.md, confirmed 2026-08-18 via AskUserQuestion -- NOT the 0-33/33-66/66-100 scheme raised earlier in conversation and then not used).

pylon_ticket_tone.source: Sourced via direct Pylon search_issues filtered to a confirmed exact account_id (resolved via search_accounts by domain/name, NOT the fuzzy account-name partial-match filter -- that filter was tested and found to cross-contaminate results across unrelated companies sharing generic name tokens, e.g. a 'Western Wealth' search surfaced 'Howard Management Group' and 'Group Fox Management' tickets; verified via get_issue on 3 sample tickets before trusting any count). States new/waiting_on_you/waiting_on_customer/on_hold, trailing ~90 days (created_after 2026-05-20). Counted only tickets flagging real PM-facing friction (tagged Escalated/Records Escalations, or title containing integration/config/migration/escalation/SOP/backlog-type keywords) per the account-health-weekly-review skill's PM-vs-renter title filter rule -- excludes the large majority of tickets, which are routine individual-applicant screening actions (income verification, co-applicants, ID disputes) and not a signal of PM relationship health. Classification: 0 friction tickets=Positive/Green, 1-2=Neutral/Yellow, 3+=Negative/Red. CAVEAT: raw-count based, not normalized by account ticket volume -- larger accounts (e.g. Beztak, McKinley, Highmark) are mechanically more likely to cross the 3+ threshold even at an equivalent underlying friction rate. This is an approximate keyword-based proxy for Tatiana's documented methodology, not a literal reproduction of undisclosed exact logic.

composite_score_partial.methodology: PARTIAL composite -- 16 of 19 rubric rows have real current data (the 3 missing rows -- Business goals, KPIs, NPS -- are listed in rows_missing_no_current_data; NPS has real data for only 7/20 accounts, all historical/pre-quarter). performance_review_cadence, executive_sponsor_alignment, and csm_qualitative_risk_flag were added 2026-08-18 (Gong-derived for the first two, HubSpot churn_risk__c for the third per Emma's direction); gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone were added 2026-08-18 (direct Gong API brief-reading and Pylon exact-account-id issue search, respectively, per Emma's sourcing direction from the account-health-weekly-review skill doc) -- see per-account 'note'/'source' fields on each for methodology caveats, several of which are best-effort proxies, not confirmed ground truth (in particular: gong_call_sentiment is unscored/None for 6 accounts with zero domain-matched Gong calls in the window -- a coverage gap, not a confirmed negative; pylon_ticket_tone is a raw-count-based proxy not normalized by account ticket volume, so larger accounts are mechanically more likely to land Red). Weight redistributed proportionally among available rows only (weights re-normalized to sum to rows_included_weight_sum, not literally 100). Per-metric scoring: Green=100/Yellow=50/Red=0, weighted average, per the pre-existing account-health-weekly-review skill's formula that this rubric explicitly carries forward. Floor rule (same skill), changed 2026-08-19 per Emma's direction to stop collapsing the displayed number: exactly 1 Red-banded row among those included still forces band=Yellow, and 2+ Red rows still forces band=Red, regardless of what the weighted math alone would say -- but as of 2026-08-19 'value' is ALWAYS the true weighted average, never overridden to a flat 50 or 0. This means a Red-banded account can show a value anywhere in 0-100 (e.g. a Red account with mostly-Green rows but 2 Red ones might still show in the 70s) -- the number is for relative severity/triage, the band is the categorical gate. (Previously, 2026-08-18 through 2026-08-19 morning: value WAS forced to a flat 0/50 to match the band -- changed after Emma flagged that this made every Red account look identical.) Decision Override Rate's Red band does NOT count toward this floor for SMB accounts, per the rubric's explicit 'not gated' rule for that segment. Bands when no floor applies: Green >=80, Yellow 60-79, Red <60 (matches both the rubric xlsx Overview tab and the skill's SKILL.md, confirmed 2026-08-18 via AskUserQuestion -- NOT the 0-33/33-66/66-100 scheme raised earlier in conversation and then not used).

median_ttd_hours.source: Sigma Core (Data Model), Groups BI (xv3TuuWX8Z), direct query -- GROUP_IS_DECISIONED=true AND GROUP_DECISIONED_AT >= 2026-07-01, median(TIME_TO_DECISION_HOURS) split by GROUP_STATUS. Corrected 2026-08-18: previously sourced from QBR Canonical Tables workbook's 'Decisioned Date Anchor' element, which is pre-aggregated and can't actually reproduce a per-group median (its own metric formulas throw column-not-found errors against that element) -- this direct-table path is now the standard.
median_ttd_hours.declined_qa_hold_diagnostic: 114/187 (61.0%) of declines show a >1h gap between Findigs' own UW decision and the final decision -- a proxy for customer-QA-hold time, NOT the same as the qa_pct row below (different metric, different definition). See project memory for the Beztak investigation this came from.
median_ttd_hours.median_note: Blended median across ALL decisioned groups this quarter (approved+declined+cancelled+passed), for reference only -- NOT what the rubric bands on. The rubric scores 'worse_of_two' (max of the approved-only and declined-only medians) specifically so a slow-decline problem can't hide behind fast, high-volume approvals.

approval_rate_pct.source: Sigma Core (Data Model), Groups BI, direct query, same population as TTD above.

override_rate_pct.source: Sigma Core (Data Model), Groups BI 'Has Decision Override' (W6x8udeWRR), direct query. Refreshed 2026-08-18 -- denominator/numerator reflect today's decisioned-this-quarter population, which grows daily; small movement vs. any earlier snapshot is expected QTD accrual, not a data error. Bands (ENT/MM): Green <=3%, Yellow 3-6%, Red >6% (reverse-engineered from the existing banded values across all 20 accounts, not a directly-quoted rubric threshold -- treat as provisional like the support-ticket-ratio recalibration). SMB is exempted from this row's normal banding entirely (shown Green regardless of value) per the rubric's explicit 'not gated' rule for that segment.
override_rate_pct.split_note: These two rows are NOT a decomposition of the blended rate above -- verified 2026-08-18 that they don't sum to it (e.g. Bridge Tower: blended=8 but approval+decline directional flags=0+0; Highmark: blended=7 but directional flags sum to 89). The blended 'Has Decision Override' flag also fires when Findigs' internal UW recommendation disagreed with the group's final status even if the group's own visible status never flipped -- something these two directional fields can't see. These are a different, narrower lens (did the group's own recorded outcome flip declined->approved, or approved->declined), not officially banded (no Green/Yellow/Red threshold has been defined for either direction individually) -- shown as raw rate/count only. Sourced from Sigma Core (Data Model), Groups BI: 'Group Is Decision Outcome Declined to Approved' (approval override) and 'Group Is Decision Outcome Approved to Declined' (decline override), same population as the blended row (GROUP_IS_DECISIONED=true AND GROUP_DECISIONED_AT >= 2026-07-01).

Counted only tickets flagging real PM-facing friction (tagged Escalated/Records Escalations, or title containing integration/config/migration/escalation/SOP/backlog-type keywords) per the account-health-weekly-review skill's PM-vs-renter title filter rule -- excludes the large majority of tickets, which are routine individual-applicant screening actions (income verification, co-applicants, ID disputes) and not a signal of PM relationship health. Classification: 0 friction tickets=Positive/Green, 1-2=Neutral/Yellow, 3+=Negative/Red. CAVEAT: raw-count based, not normalized by account ticket volume -- larger accounts (e.g. Beztak, McKinley, Highmark) are mechanically more likely to cross the 3+ threshold even at an equivalent underlying friction rate. This is an approximate keyword-based proxy for Tatiana's documented methodology, not a literal reproduction of undisclosed exact logic.

composite_score_partial.methodology: PARTIAL composite -- 16 of 19 rubric rows have real current data (the 3 missing rows -- Business goals, KPIs, NPS -- are listed in rows_missing_no_current_data; NPS has real data for only 7/20 accounts, all historical/pre-quarter). performance_review_cadence, executive_sponsor_alignment, and csm_qualitative_risk_flag were added 2026-08-18 (Gong-derived for the first two, HubSpot churn_risk__c for the third per Emma's direction); gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone were added 2026-08-18 (direct Gong API brief-reading and Pylon exact-account-id issue search, respectively, per Emma's sourcing direction from the account-health-weekly-review skill doc) -- see per-account 'note'/'source' fields on each for methodology caveats, several of which are best-effort proxies, not confirmed ground truth (in particular: gong_call_sentiment is unscored/None for 6 accounts with zero domain-matched Gong calls in the window -- a coverage gap, not a confirmed negative; pylon_ticket_tone is a raw-count-based proxy not normalized by account ticket volume, so larger accounts are mechanically more likely to land Red). Weight redistributed proportionally among available rows only (weights re-normalized to sum to rows_included_weight_sum, not literally 100). Per-metric scoring: Green=100/Yellow=50/Red=0, weighted average, per the pre-existing account-health-weekly-review skill's formula that this rubric explicitly carries forward. (Previously, 2026-08-18 through 2026-08-19 morning: value WAS forced to a flat 0/50 to match the band -- changed after Emma flagged that this made every Red account look identical.) Decision Override Rate's Red band does NOT count toward this floor for SMB accounts, per the rubric's explicit 'not gated' rule for that segment. Bands when no floor applies: Green >=80, Yellow 60-79, Red <60 (matches both the rubric xlsx Overview tab and the skill's SKILL.md, confirmed 2026-08-18 via AskUserQuestion -- NOT the 0-33/33-66/66-100 scheme raised earlier in conversation and then not used).

performance_review_cadence.source: Derived from Gong call titles, trailing 90 days (2026-05-20 to 2026-08-18), matched to account by external-party email domain (not name-fragment keyword matching -- several account names are generic English words/surnames -- Western, Standard, Jones, Brick, Open House, Oakwood -- that would false-positive under substring matching, the same failure class already caught in the Pylon ticket-tone company mismatch). (Previously, 2026-08-18 through 2026-08-19 morning: value WAS forced to a flat 0/50 to match the band -- changed after Emma flagged that this made every Red account look identical.) Decision Override Rate's Red band does NOT count toward this floor for SMB accounts, per the rubric's explicit 'not gated' rule for that segment. Bands when no floor applies: Green >=80, Yellow 60-79, Red <60 (matches both the rubric xlsx Overview tab and the skill's SKILL.md, confirmed 2026-08-18 via AskUserQuestion -- NOT the 0-33/33-66/66-100 scheme raised earlier in conversation and then not used).

pylon_ticket_tone.source: Sourced via direct Pylon search_issues filtered to a confirmed exact account_id (resolved via search_accounts by domain/name, NOT the fuzzy account-name partial-match filter -- that filter was tested and found to cross-contaminate results across unrelated companies sharing generic name tokens, e.g. a 'Western Wealth' search surfaced 'Howard Management Group' and 'Group Fox Management' tickets; verified via get_issue on 3 sample tickets before trusting any count). States new/waiting_on_you/waiting_on_customer/on_hold, trailing ~90 days (created_after 2026-05-20). Counted only tickets flagging real PM-facing friction (tagged Escalated/Records Escalations, or title containing integration/config/migration/escalation/SOP/backlog-type keywords) per the account-health-weekly-review skill's PM-vs-renter title filter rule -- excludes the large majority of tickets, which are routine individual-applicant screening actions (income verification, co-applicants, ID disputes) and not a signal of PM relationship health. Classification: 0 friction tickets=Positive/Green, 1-2=Neutral/Yellow, 3+=Negative/Red. CAVEAT: raw-count based, not normalized by account ticket volume -- larger accounts (e.g. Beztak, McKinley, Highmark) are mechanically more likely to cross the 3+ threshold even at an equivalent underlying friction rate. This is an approximate keyword-based proxy for Tatiana's documented methodology, not a literal reproduction of undisclosed exact logic.

composite_score_partial.methodology: PARTIAL composite -- 16 of 19 rubric rows have real current data (the 3 missing rows -- Business goals, KPIs, NPS -- are listed in rows_missing_no_current_data; NPS has real data for only 7/20 accounts, all historical/pre-quarter). performance_review_cadence, executive_sponsor_alignment, and csm_qualitative_risk_flag were added 2026-08-18 (Gong-derived for the first two, HubSpot churn_risk__c for the third per Emma's direction); gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone were added 2026-08-18 (direct Gong API brief-reading and Pylon exact-account-id issue search, respectively, per Emma's sourcing direction from the account-health-weekly-review skill doc) -- see per-account 'note'/'source' fields on each for methodology caveats, several of which are best-effort proxies, not confirmed ground truth (in particular: gong_call_sentiment is unscored/None for 6 accounts with zero domain-matched Gong calls in the window -- a coverage gap, not a confirmed negative; pylon_ticket_tone is a raw-count-based proxy not normalized by account ticket volume, so larger accounts are mechanically more likely to land Red). Weight redistributed proportionally among available rows only (weights re-normalized to sum to rows_included_weight_sum, not literally 100). Per-metric scoring: Green=100/Yellow=50/Red=0, weighted average, per the pre-existing account-health-weekly-review skill's formula that this rubric explicitly carries forward. Floor rule (same skill), changed 2026-08-19 per Emma's direction to stop collapsing the displayed number: exactly 1 Red-banded row among those included still forces band=Yellow, and 2+ Red rows still forces band=Red, regardless of what the weighted math alone would say -- but as of 2026-08-19 'value' is ALWAYS the true weighted average, never overridden to a flat 50 or 0. This means a Red-banded account can show a value anywhere in 0-100 (e.g. a Red account with mostly-Green rows but 2 Red ones might still show in the 70s) -- the number is for relative severity/triage, the band is the categorical gate. (Previously, 2026-08-18 through 2026-08-19 morning: value WAS forced to a flat 0/50 to match the band -- changed after Emma flagged that this made every Red account look identical.) Decision Override Rate's Red band does NOT count toward this floor for SMB accounts, per the rubric's explicit 'not gated' rule for that segment. Bands when no floor applies: Green >=80, Yellow 60-79, Red <60 (matches both the rubric xlsx Overview tab and the skill's SKILL.md, confirmed 2026-08-18 via AskUserQuestion -- NOT the 0-33/33-66/66-100 scheme raised earlier in conversation and then not used).

gong_call_sentiment.source: Sourced via direct Gong REST API (not the stale Salesforce Gong__Gong_Call__c sync, confirmed 5+ weeks behind as of 2026-08-18), domain-matched to account, trailing 90 days. Classified by reading each matched call's AI-generated brief against the account-health-weekly-review skill's 3-tier definition (Positive=milestones confirmed/proactive/no escalations, Neutral=routine sync/no strong signal, Negative=friction/frustration/unresolved bugs/Findigs blamed/competitor pressure). Accounts with zero domain-matched Gong calls in the window are left unscored (None) rather than assumed negative -- a coverage gap in domain-matching is not evidence of silence. 'thin' accounts had very few matched calls (1-3), so the classification rests on a small sample.

pylon_ticket_tone.source: Sourced via direct Pylon search_issues filtered to a confirmed exact account_id (resolved via search_accounts by domain/name, NOT the fuzzy account-name partial-match filter -- that filter was tested and found to cross-contaminate results across unrelated companies sharing generic name tokens, e.g. a 'Western Wealth' search surfaced 'Howard Management Group' and 'Group Fox Management' tickets; verified via get_issue on 3 sample tickets before trusting any count). States new/waiting_on_you/waiting_on_customer/on_hold, trailing ~90 days (created_after 2026-05-20). Counted only tickets flagging real PM-facing friction (tagged Escalated/Records Escalations, or title containing integration/config/migration/escalation/SOP/backlog-type keywords) per the account-health-weekly-review skill's PM-vs-renter title filter rule -- excludes the large majority of tickets, which are routine individual-applicant screening actions (income verification, co-applicants, ID disputes) and not a signal of PM relationship health. Classification: 0 friction tickets=Positive/Green, 1-2=Neutral/Yellow, 3+=Negative/Red. CAVEAT: raw-count based, not normalized by account ticket volume -- larger accounts (e.g. Beztak, McKinley, Highmark) are mechanically more likely to cross the 3+ threshold even at an equivalent underlying friction rate. This is an approximate keyword-based proxy for Tatiana's documented methodology, not a literal reproduction of undisclosed exact logic.

composite_score_partial.methodology: PARTIAL composite -- 16 of 19 rubric rows have real current data (the 3 missing rows -- Business goals, KPIs, NPS -- are listed in rows_missing_no_current_data; NPS has real data for only 7/20 accounts, all historical/pre-quarter). performance_review_cadence, executive_sponsor_alignment, and csm_qualitative_risk_flag were added 2026-08-18 (Gong-derived for the first two, HubSpot churn_risk__c for the third per Emma's direction); gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone were added 2026-08-18 (direct Gong API brief-reading and Pylon exact-account-id issue search, respectively, per Emma's sourcing direction from the account-health-weekly-review skill doc) -- see per-account 'note'/'source' fields on each for methodology caveats, several of which are best-effort proxies, not confirmed ground truth (in particular: gong_call_sentiment is unscored/None for 6 accounts with zero domain-matched Gong calls in the window -- a coverage gap, not a confirmed negative; pylon_ticket_tone is a raw-count-based proxy not normalized by account ticket volume, so larger accounts are mechanically more likely to land Red). Weight redistributed proportionally among available rows only (weights re-normalized to sum to rows_included_weight_sum, not literally 100). Per-metric scoring: Green=100/Yellow=50/Red=0, weighted average, per the pre-existing account-health-weekly-review skill's formula that this rubric explicitly carries forward. Floor rule (same skill), changed 2026-08-19 per Emma's direction to stop collapsing the displayed number: exactly 1 Red-banded row among those included still forces band=Yellow, and 2+ Red rows still forces band=Red, regardless of what the weighted math alone would say -- but as of 2026-08-19 'value' is ALWAYS the true weighted average, never overridden to a flat 50 or 0. This means a Red-banded account can show a value anywhere in 0-100 (e.g. a Red account with mostly-Green rows but 2 Red ones might still show in the 70s) -- the number is for relative severity/triage, the band is the categorical gate. (Previously, 2026-08-18 through 2026-08-19 morning: value WAS forced to a flat 0/50 to match the band -- changed after Emma flagged that this made every Red account look identical.) Decision Override Rate's Red band does NOT count toward this floor for SMB accounts, per the rubric's explicit 'not gated' rule for that segment. Bands when no floor applies: Green >=80, Yellow 60-79, Red <60 (matches both the rubric xlsx Overview tab and the skill's SKILL.md, confirmed 2026-08-18 via AskUserQuestion -- NOT the 0-33/33-66/66-100 scheme raised earlier in conversation and then not used).

composite_score_partial.methodology: PARTIAL composite -- 16 of 19 rubric rows have real current data (the 3 missing rows -- Business goals, KPIs, NPS -- are listed in rows_missing_no_current_data; NPS has real data for only 7/20 accounts, all historical/pre-quarter). performance_review_cadence, executive_sponsor_alignment, and csm_qualitative_risk_flag were added 2026-08-18 (Gong-derived for the first two, HubSpot churn_risk__c for the third per Emma's direction); gong_call_sentiment and pylon_ticket_tone were added 2026-08-18 (direct Gong API brief-reading and Pylon exact-account-id issue search, respectively, per Emma's sourcing direction from the account-health-weekly-review skill doc) -- see per-account 'note'/'source' fields on each for methodology caveats, several of which are best-effort proxies, not confirmed ground truth (in particular: gong_call_sentiment is unscored/None for 6 accounts with zero domain-matched Gong calls in the window -- a coverage gap, not a confirmed negative; pylon_ticket_tone is a raw-count-based proxy not normalized by account ticket volume, so larger accounts are mechanically more likely to land Red). Weight redistributed proportionally among available rows only (weights re-normalized to sum to rows_included_weight_sum, not literally 100). Per-metric scoring: Green=100/Yellow=50/Red=0, weighted average, per the pre-existing account-health-weekly-review skill's formula that this rubric explicitly carries forward. Floor rule (same skill), changed 2026-08-19 per Emma's direction to stop collapsing the displayed number: exactly 1 Red-banded row among those included still forces band=Yellow, and 2+ Red rows still forces band=Red, regardless of what the weighted math alone would say -- but as of 2026-08-19 'value' is ALWAYS the true weighted average, never overridden to a flat 50 or 0. This means a Red-banded account can show a value anywhere in 0-100 (e.g. a Red account with mostly-Green rows but 2 Red ones might still show in the 70s) -- the number is for relative severity/triage, the band is the categorical gate. (Previously, 2026-08-18 through 2026-08-19 morning: value WAS forced to a flat 0/50 to match the band -- changed after Emma flagged that this made every Red account look identical.) Decision Override Rate's Red band does NOT count toward this floor for SMB accounts, per the rubric's explicit 'not gated' rule for that segment. Bands when no floor applies: Green >=80, Yellow 60-79, Red <60 (matches both the rubric xlsx Overview tab and the skill's SKILL.md, confirmed 2026-08-18 via AskUserQuestion -- NOT the 0-33/33-66/66-100 scheme raised earlier in conversation and then not used).

Floor rule: exactly 1 red-gating row forces band=Yellow, 2+ forces band=Red, regardless of the weighted value -- but 'value' is always the true weighted average, never overridden to a flat 50/0. composite_score_partial.methodology: Composite across all 3 pillars (Platform & Product Metrics, Strategic Alignment/Governance, Client Sentiment) -- Phase 3 qualitative matching completed 2026-08-26 for this account (HubSpot company match + Gong domain/brief matching + Pylon account_id ticket matching). 14 of 19 rubric rows have real current data; the 3 permanently missing rows are listed in rows_missing_no_current_data. Weight redistributed proportionally among available rows only (re-normalized to rows_included_weight_sum, not literally 100). Per-metric scoring: Green=100/Yellow=50/Red=0, weighted average. Floor rule: exactly 1 red-gating row forces band=Yellow, 2+ forces band=Red, regardless of the weighted value -- but 'value' is always the true weighted average, never overridden to a flat 50/0. Decision Override Rate's Red does not gate for SMB accounts; Approval Rate's Red does not gate for Full-Screen service type -- both per the rubric's explicit exemptions.

composite_score_partial.methodology: Composite across all 3 pillars (Platform & Product Metrics, Strategic Alignment/Governance, Client Sentiment) -- Phase 3 qualitative matching completed 2026-08-26 for this account (HubSpot company match + Gong domain/brief matching + Pylon account_id ticket matching). 10 of 19 rubric rows have real current data; the 3 permanently missing rows are listed in rows_missing_no_current_data. Weight redistributed proportionally among available rows only (re-normalized to rows_included_weight_sum, not literally 100). Per-metric scoring: Green=100/Yellow=50/Red=0, weighted average. Floor rule: exactly 1 red-gating row forces band=Yellow, 2+ forces band=Red, regardless of the weighted value -- but 'value' is always the true weighted average, never overridden to a flat 50/0. Decision Override Rate's Red does not gate for SMB accounts; Approval Rate's Red does not gate for Full-Screen service type -- both per the rubric's explicit exemptions.

Floor rule: exactly 1 red-gating row forces band=Yellow, 2+ forces band=Red, regardless of the weighted value -- but 'value' is always the true weighted average, never overridden to a flat 50/0. Decision Override Rate's Red does not gate for SMB accounts; Approval Rate's Red does not gate for Full-Screen service type -- both per the rubric's explicit exemptions.
